findings.description: The new `components` filter excludes only CONTROL, BARE, absent and eval_only arms, so a0_bare_fable becomes a 'component' with a keep/remove decision against a1_full. The suite comment introduced in the same diff describes a0_bare_fable as 'A0 on the review model', i.e. a third baseline, and the report comment on this very line says components are 'every runnable arm but the two baselines'. A bare-model baseline is not a shipped-default component: the report will emit a nonsensical decision row ('remove a0_bare_fable' / 'keep a0_bare_fable'), inflate k in the expected-false-positive sentence (9 instead of 8), and the AR-12 / decisions-length tests lock that in.
findings.failure_mode: Report output misrepresents a baseline arm as an ablatable component; decision table contains a meaningless row and the stated false-positive budget is computed over the wrong k.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude bare-model baselines from components explicitly (e.g. `a.get('toggles', {}).get('loa_mount') is False` or a `baseline: true` suite flag mirroring `eval_only`), keep a0_bare_fable in the rendered comparison tables, and update AR-12 / the decisions-length assertion to 8.

findings.description: TOGGLE_VALUES hard-codes the toggle vocabulary and each toggle's accepted values as a second copy of what lib/sandbox-mount.sh apply_arm_toggles implements, even though validate-suite.sh already sources lib/sandbox-mount.sh a few lines above (the `shellcheck source=lib/sandbox-mount.sh` pushd). The took_effect rule set in the same change is derived from took-effect.sh by parsing; the toggle set is not. A new toggle or value added to apply_arm_toggles (or to pipeline-run.sh's hand-built dry-run edit list, which the primary reviewer already flagged) will pass the pipeline but be rejected by the validator, or vice versa, with no test to catch the drift.
findings.failure_mode: Validator and runtime disagree on which toggles/values exist; a legitimately supported arm is rejected by validate-suite.sh, or an unsupported toggle silently validates and is ignored at run time.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the vocabulary from lib/sandbox-mount.sh (e.g. an `ARM_TOGGLE_VOCAB` associative array or a `print_toggle_vocab` function) and feed it to the Python validator the same way RULE_IDS is passed, or add a test that asserts TOGGLE_VALUES equals the keys apply_arm_toggles dispatches on.
